examples.title: Guess the number
examples.description: A real three-attempt text game with high/low hints and a fixed secret of seven.
examples.source:
let guess = 0
let won = 0
say "Guess the secret whole number. You have three tries."
repeat 3 times
 if won == 0
  ask number guess "Your guess?"
  if guess == 7
   say "You found it!"
   set won = 1
  else
   if guess < 7
    say "Try a larger number."
   else
    say "Try a smaller number."
   end
  end
 end
end
if won == 0
 say "The secret was 7. Try again next time."
end

examples.title: Thermostat lab
examples.description: Try three readings and see why a heater should not flicker around one temperature.
examples.source:
let temperature = 0
let heating = 0
say "Thermostat simulation: three whole Celsius readings, 0 to 60."
repeat 3 times
 ask number temperature "Temperature?"
 if temperature > 60
  say "Outside this lesson range. State unchanged."
 else
  if temperature < 18
   set heating = 1
  end
  if temperature > 24
   set heating = 0
  end
  if heating == 1
   say "Heater on."
  else
   say "Heater off."
  end
 end
end

concepts.meaning: A remembered value lets a later decision depend on what happened before.
A boundary that changes a decision.
Different on/off boundaries prevent rapid switching near a single boundary.

examples.scope: A console decision simulation, not a sensor reader, hardware controller or safety system.
instructions: Run with 17, 20, 25 on separate lines. The middle reading keeps the previous heater state.
Clear the answer box to answer each question yourself.
Try 18, 24, 61. The first two boundaries hold state; 61 is rejected by this lesson without changing it.

examples.title: Grid rover
examples.description: Steer a little rover without leaving its four-by-four world.
examples.source:
let x = 0
let y = 0
let command = 0
say "Grid rover: start 0,0. Edges are 0 to 3. Six turns."
say "1 east, 2 west, 3 north, 4 south."
repeat 6 times
 ask number command "Direction?"
 if command == 1
  if x < 3
   set x = x + 1
  else
   say "East wall. Stay here."
  end
 end
 if command == 2
  if x > 0
   set x = x - 1
  else
   say "West wall. Stay here."
  end
 end
 if command == 3
  if y < 3
   set y = y + 1
  else
   say "North wall. Stay here."
  end
 end
 if command == 4
  if y > 0
   set y = y - 1
  else
   say "South wall. Stay here."
  end
 end
 if command < 1
  say "Choose 1 to 4. Stay here."
 end
 if command > 4
  say "Choose 1 to 4. Stay here."
 end
 say "x:"
 show x
 say "y:"
 show y
end
if x == 3
 if y == 3
  say "You reached the beacon!"
 end
end

concepts.meaning: x measures sideways and y measures upwards.
Check a condition before changing a value.
Run the enclosed steps a fixed number of times.

challenge.prompt: Reach the beacon from another starting position.
challenge.hint: Change the first x and y values, then plan six directions.

instructions: Run the six supplied directions to reach 3,3.
Use 2 at the start to try a wall. The coordinate stays zero; subtraction is never attempted below zero.
Each turn displays the new x and y. Invalid directions consume a turn and leave the position unchanged.

examples.title: Tiny vending shop
examples.description: Keep credit, refuse an early purchase and return unused coins.
examples.source:
let action = 0
let credit = 0
let sold = 0
say "Vending simulation: four turns. A snack costs 100 cents."
say "1 add 50 cents, 2 buy, 3 cancel."
repeat 4 times
 ask number action "Action?"
 if action == 1
  set credit = credit + 50
  say "Added 50 cents."
 end
 if action == 2
  if credit >= 100
   set credit = credit - 100
   set sold = sold + 1
   say "Snack dispensed."
  else
   say "Not enough credit. Nothing charged."
  end
 end
 if action == 3
  say "Refund in cents:"
  show credit
  set credit = 0
 end
 if action < 1
  say "Choose 1, 2 or 3. Credit unchanged."
 end
 if action > 3
  say "Choose 1, 2 or 3. Credit unchanged."
 end
 say "Credit in cents:"
 show credit
end
say "Final refund in cents:"
show credit
set credit = 0
say "Snacks sold:"
show sold

concepts.meaning: Only subtract the price after confirming enough credit.
A sequence of choices updates remembered state.
Whole cents avoid decimal rounding in this small lesson.

challenge.prompt: Try cancelling after adding money.
challenge.hint: Use answers 1, 3, 2, 0. Confirm that the cancelled money cannot buy a snack.

examples.scope: A four-turn console simulation. It has no payment gateway, real money, stock database or physical vending device.
instructions: Each action uses one of four turns.
The supplied answers try to buy too early, add two coins, then buy successfully.
Unused credit is displayed as a final refund and cleared. No actual money changes hands.

examples.title: Lighthouse escape
examples.description: Make three choices, keep a key and unlock the lighthouse door.
examples.source:
let choice = 0
let key = 0
let escaped = 0
say "Lighthouse escape. You have three turns."
say "1 search the desk, 2 try the door, 3 look at the sea."
repeat 3 times
 if escaped == 0
  ask number choice "Your choice?"
  if choice == 1
   if key == 0
    set key = 1
    say "You found a brass key."
   else
    say "The desk is empty now."
   end
  end
  if choice == 2
   if key == 1
    set escaped = 1
    say "The door opens. You are free!"
   else
    say "Locked. Maybe there is a key nearby."
   end
  end
  if choice == 3
   say "A boat is waiting beyond the locked door."
  end
  if choice < 1
   say "Choose 1, 2 or 3."
  end
  if choice > 3
   say "Choose 1, 2 or 3."
  end
 end
end
if escaped == 0
 say "The tide rose. Reset and try a different plan."
end

concepts.meaning: The key and escaped values remember the story so far.
A choice can depend on another condition, such as having the key.
The story ends after a limited number of choices.

challenge.prompt: Add a clue to the sea message that helps a new player.
challenge.hint: Edit the words inside the choice 3 say line.

examples.scope: An authored branching console story, not an AI-generated story service.
instructions: Choose 1 to find a key and 2 to open the door.
The supplied journey first tries a locked door, then finds the key and returns.
A successful escape stops asking questions even if turns remain.

examples.title: Can I book this room?
examples.description: Check whether two same-day whole-hour room intervals overlap.
examples.source:
fn overlap(a,b,c,d)
 return (a < d) * (c < b)
end
ask number start "Existing start hour, 0 to 23?"
ask number finish "Existing finish hour, 1 to 24?"
ask number wanted "Requested start hour, 0 to 23?"
ask number until "Requested finish hour, 1 to 24?"
let valid = 1
if start >= finish
 set valid = 0
end
if wanted >= until
 set valid = 0
end
if finish > 24
 set valid = 0
end
if until > 24
 set valid = 0
end
if valid == 0
 say "Use a start before a finish, within one day ending at 24."
else
 if overlap(start,finish,wanted,until)
  say "Conflict. Choose a different time."
 else
  say "No overlap. These two intervals can share the room."
 end
end

concepts.meaning: A booking includes its start but not its finish; another may start exactly when it ends.
Give a reusable calculation a name.
Reject an invalid request before making a decision.

challenge.prompt: Change the requested time so it overlaps the existing booking.
challenge.hint: Try 10 to 12 against 9 to 11, then try 11 to 12.

examples.scope: One existing interval and one request, using whole hours on the same day. No actual reservation, persistence, dates, time zones or simultaneous booking protection.
instructions: Enter four answers: existing start, existing finish, requested start, requested finish.
Hours are nonnegative whole numbers. Start must be before finish; finish cannot exceed 24.
The supplied journey shows that a booking ending at 11 does not conflict with one starting at 11.

examples.title: Pocket pet
examples.description: Look after a tiny pet whose energy changes with each choice.
examples.source:
let energy = 4
let fun = 0
let action = 0
say "Pocket pet: four turns. Energy starts at 4 and stops at 6."
say "1 feed, 2 play, 3 rest."
repeat 4 times
 ask number action "What shall we do?"
 if action == 1
  if energy < 6
   set energy = energy + 1
   say "Yum! Energy increased."
  else
   say "Already full."
  end
 end
 if action == 2
  if energy >= 3
   set energy = energy - 3
   set fun = fun + 1
   say "That was fun!"
  else
   say "Too tired to play. Feed or rest first."
  end
 end
 if action == 3
  set energy = 6
  say "Rested. Energy is full."
 end
 if action < 1
  say "Choose 1, 2 or 3. Nothing changed."
 end
 if action > 3
  say "Choose 1, 2 or 3. Nothing changed."
 end
 say "Energy:"
 show energy
end
say "Happy play times:"
show fun

concepts.meaning: A tired pet cannot spend energy it does not have.
The energy and fun values change as the game continues.
The feed rule keeps energy at or below six.

challenge.prompt: Find a four-turn plan with three happy play times.
challenge.hint: Try play, rest, play, play. Rest sets energy to six.

examples.scope: A deterministic turn-based console game. No animation, clock, AI behaviour or saved pet data is implied.
instructions: Choose 1 to feed, 2 to play or 3 to rest. Each choice uses one turn.
Playing costs three energy; feeding adds one up to six; resting fills it to six.
The supplied journey shows a refused play, then recovery through rest.
